children: Australia's economy slowed in the June quarter as rising borrowing costs and high fuel prices dampened consumer demand, yet analysts fear a deeper downturn will be needed to tame stubborn inflation.
Data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics on Wednesday showed real gross domestic product (GDP) rose a moderate 0.4% in the second quarter, just above market forecasts of a 0.3% gain.

Annual growth dropped to 2.1%, from 2.5%, but topped forecasts of 1.8% due to past revisions. The slowdown has been largely engineered by the Reserve Bank of Australia, which has lifted interest rates three times this year in an attempt to curb inflation but with limited success.
